area: Rendering, safety and failure states (app.js render paths, innerHTML sinks, load failures, NaN/Infinity on the page, tile/chip/table count consistency)
summary:
On the shipped data the page renders cleanly. Headless Chromium showed no uncaught errors, 0 console errors and no NaN, undefined or Infinity on the page. The counts agree: the tile says 10, the All chip says 10, the table has 10 rows, and the area chips sum to 3+1+2+2+2. Outside that dataset the page fails in ways that hide alerts or show a false all-clear. All of these were reproduced in Node against the real app.js (DOM stub plus tiny inline CSVs: 20 defect cases MISMATCH, 3 controls MATCH) and in headless Chromium (30 scenarios).

(1) HIGH. The tiles render before the exception table, and the yearling tile looks up a group literally named "Yearlings". If that group is missing (for example a cow-calf-only ranch), if a group name is all digits, or if groups.csv is empty, the tile code throws and the alert table is never drawn. The header still says "Data as of September 30, 2026 at 6:00 PM".

(2) HIGH. There is no load-failure handling: no response.ok check and no catch. A 404, a network abort or a header-only file for pastures, moves, weights, water or meta gives an uncaught TypeError and a page of empty cards with no message.

(3) HIGH. A missing or empty health.csv (or budget.csv), or an empty water.csv, produces a silent all-clear: "Health (0)" and "Nothing in health needs attention." while the overdue booster disappears.

(4) MEDIUM. CSV text reaches innerHTML unescaped in 9 places. Script from a pasture name, ear tag or group name ran on load, script in a tag ran on tooltip hover, and one payload deleted every alert row while the chips still read "All (10)".

(5) MEDIUM. A tank with no reading in the last 7 days crashes the water charts and everything drawn after them (grazing, gain, budget, rules).

(6) MEDIUM. Infinity and NaN reach the display: "Infinity% over season to date", a budget chart drawn with NaN coordinates, "−NaN%", "$NaN of $NaN".

(7) MEDIUM. A blank level reading becomes a critical leak alert, "Dropped 70 points in 24 hours, now %".

Low findings:
- The "Water tanks OK" tile undercounts when tank ids contain a space.
- The empty states read "Nothing in all needs attention." and "−0.0%".
- Keyboard focus is lost after a chip is activated.
- Tooltips go off-screen on a phone.
- The grazing timeline's month lines are hard-coded to June–September 2026.
trace:
LOAD (app.js:221): Promise.all fetches the 8 files data/<f>.csv and calls parseCSV(await res.text()). It never checks res.ok and has no catch. On a 404, python http.server's HTML body is parsed as CSV: 12 rows keyed "<!DOCTYPE HTML>" (render.repro R05: "parseCSV(404 body) -> 12 rows with keys [\"<!DOCTYPE HTML>\"]"). The code is a top-level await in a module, so any throw becomes an uncaught error and the page shows nothing about it.

RULES (app.js:222 findExceptions): this throws for missing or empty pastures, moves (404), weights (404), water (404) and meta. Because line 223 never runs, the asof line stays "" and only the static headings are left.

ASOF (app.js:223): written with textContent, so it is safe.

RENDER ORDER (app.js:225): tiles, then exceptionsTable, waterMultiples, grazingTimeline, gainStrip, budget, rules. The calls are synchronous and not isolated from each other, so a throw in one stops all the later ones.

TILES (app.js:44-58), written with innerHTML:
- Needs attention = exc.length, plus counts by severity.
- Head on grass = the sum of groups.head, plus the group names (CSV text).
- Water tanks OK = tanks.length minus the size of the set of e.subject.split(" ")[1] over the Water rows. The tank id is parsed back out of the display text.
- Yearling gain = gainStatus().find(group === "Yearlings").adg and .target.toFixed. The group name is hard-coded.
- Spend vs budget = (ta−tb)/tb with no zero guard. The sign is "−" whenever ta <= tb.

EXCEPTION TABLE (app.js:61-70):
- The chips come from the constant AREAS, with counts from exc.
- Each row is badge(sev) (constant) + area (constant) + e.subject + e.problem + e.action, joined into innerHTML.
- subject carries tank_id, pasture name, group names, health group and task, and budget category. problem carries level, tags, next_due and the weigh-in date. action is constant text.
- With no rows the table says `Nothing in ${area.toLowerCase()} needs attention.`

WATER MINIS (app.js:72-110): the h4 innerHTML holds tank id + pasture name + level. The tooltip innerHTML holds tank + pasture name + level_pct. Lines 90-93 assume at least one reading in the last 7 days (last.time).

CHARTS: SVG labels go through text(), which uses textContent and is safe. The tooltips go through hover() (app.js:28), which sets tip.innerHTML from group, pasture name and planned days (grazing, :143), tag and group (gain, :170), and category (budget, :194).

BUDGET TABLE (app.js:198): innerHTML with the category.

RULES TABLE: built from constants only.

WORKED EXAMPLE, the T4 leak:
- Source: water.csv T4 rows.
- waterStatus: the last reading is 10%. The latest reading at least 24 h older is 56%, so drop24h = 46.
- findExceptions: critical, subject "Tank T4 (Lone Tree, Heifers here now)" (whoIsThere comes from the open moves), problem "Dropped 46 points in 24 hours, now 10%", action "Check for a leak or a stuck float; haul water if it can't be fixed today".
- The row is written into #exceptions with innerHTML.
- The tile counts "T4" through subject.split(" ")[1], giving "Water tanks OK 5 of 8 | 3 need a look". The chip shows "Water (3)". The T4 mini heading shows "T4 Lone Tree10%".
- In the browser baseline every value matched: tiles "Needs attention: 10 | 2 critical, 6 serious, 2 warning"; chips "All (10)","Water (3)","Grazing (1)","Gain (2)","Health (2)","Budget (2)"; 10 rows; 0 console errors.

findings.title: Any tile error hides the whole exception table; the yearling tile requires a group literally named 'Yearlings'
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASE R11: groups/moves/weights rename Yearlings->Steers, T2 steady at 20%; CASE R12: group named 2025). Browser: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.browser.mjs <scratch> 8880 (scenarios no-yearlings, numeric-group, 404:groups, empty:groups, empty:weights)
findings.expected: The 1 alert computed by hand (T2 at 20% < 25% -> critical 'Down to 20% full') is listed. Only the yearling tile changes, e.g. to 'no Yearlings group'.
findings.actual: R11: "findExceptions -> 1 row(s); app.js error=TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'adg'); asof shown='Example Ranch (fictional), 1,200 acres in 2 pastures. Data a...'; #exceptions writes=0, rows shown=0". R12: "parseCSV group value: 2025 (number); app.js error=TypeError: g.group.toLowerCase is not a function; #exceptions writes=0". Browser no-yearlings: uncaught ["Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'adg')"], asof "...Data as of September 30, 2026 at 6:00 PM.", sections {"tiles":0,"chips":0,"exceptionTableRows":0,...,"rules":0}. The screenshot shows every card empty under the current as-of stamp.
findings.consequence: A cow-calf-only operation, or one whose groups are called 'Steers' or '2025', gets a page that looks loaded and current but has an empty 'Needs attention' card. A critical leaking tank or an overdue vaccination is never shown, and nothing says anything went wrong, so the manager can read it as an all-clear. The README invites real data ('replace the CSVs with exports in the same columns').
findings.regression_test: Move the tile computation into a pure tileModel(d, exc) function, or reuse the DOM stub in render.repro.mjs. Input: groups 'Cows' (target 0) only; water T2 readings 20/20/20 ending at as_of 2026-09-30T18:00. Assert that the table model has exactly 1 row: severity critical, subject 'Tank T2 (Windmill)', problem 'Down to 20% full'. These values are worked out by hand: 20 < 25, and the drop is 0. Assert that tileModel does not throw and that its gain tile says there is no yearling weigh-in. A second test with a group named '2025' asserts that the tile text contains '2025'.
findings.proposed_fix: Render the exception table before the tiles. Wrap each section call in try/catch and write a visible 'This section could not be drawn: <reason>' note in that section. Replace the hard-coded 'Yearlings' lookup with one gain line per group that has a target, or with the worst group against its target, and fall back to 'no weigh-ins'. Use String(g.group) before toLowerCase.

findings.title: No load-failure handling: a missing, aborted or empty CSV leaves a blank page with no message
findings.location: app.js:221-222 (no res.ok check, no catch); exceptions.js:22-34 (parseCSV accepts an HTML body); exceptions.js:43, 58, 69, 95
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASES R08 water 404, R09 meta 404/header-only, R10 fetch rejects). Browser scenarios 404:pastures|moves|weights|water|meta, abort:water, empty:pastures|meta
findings.expected: A visible banner naming the file and the problem, for example 'water.csv could not be loaded (404)'. Alerts for the other areas are still listed.
findings.actual: R08: "error=TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare'); asof=''; page tells user: false; innerHTML writes: tiles=0, exceptions=0, rules=0". R09: "404: error=TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice') ... header-only: error=TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'as_of')". R10: "error=TypeError: Failed to fetch; page tells user: false". Browser 404:water: uncaught ["Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare')"], console ["Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)"], every section count 0. abort:water: uncaught ["Failed to fetch"].
findings.consequence: When one nightly export fails or is cut off, the manager sees only the static headings with no as-of time and no error. Every alert in every area is hidden, including the ones whose files loaded fine, and finding the cause needs developer tools. Whether the deployed GitHub Pages 404 page behaves the same is inferred, not verified: the proxy refused cowcampstx.github.io.
findings.regression_test: With a stubbed fetch, water.csv returns 404 and the other files are the tiny inline set from render.repro.mjs, with a health task due 2026-09-15 and status open. Expect a banner containing 'water.csv' and '404'. Expect the table to still contain the Health row 'Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15)'. The 15 days is worked out by hand: Sep 15 to Sep 30. With fetch rejecting for budget.csv, expect a banner naming budget.csv, and expect the other areas still drawn.
findings.proposed_fix: In the loader, check res.ok and check that the header row matches the expected columns for each file. Collect the failures and show them in a banner at the top of the page. Run each area's rules separately in try/catch, and turn a failed area into a serious 'Water data unavailable: <reason>' row instead of throwing. Treat a missing or empty meta.csv as a fatal error that gets an explicit message.

findings.title: Silent all-clear when health.csv or budget.csv is missing or empty, or water.csv is empty
findings.location: exceptions.js:140-141 (rows without status are skipped), exceptions.js:82-89, app.js:46-55 (tile '0 of 0'), app.js:69 (empty message)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASES R05 health 404, R06 health header-only, R07 water header-only). Browser scenarios 404:health, empty:health, empty:water, 404:budget, empty:budget, with each chip clicked
findings.expected: The page says health or water data is missing. It does not report 'Health (0)' or 'Nothing in health needs attention.'
findings.actual: R05: "with file: 1 Health row; with 404: error=null; chip 'Health (0)'; Health filter says 'Nothing in health needs attention.'". Browser 404:health: chips ["All (8)",...,"Health (0)",...]: the overdue booster and the pinkeye check have gone, and the Health filter says "Nothing in health needs attention.". Browser empty:water: tiles "Needs attention: 7 | 0 critical, 5 serious, 2 warning" and "Water tanks OK: 0 of 0 | 0 need a look"; chips "Water (0)"; Water filter "Nothing in water needs attention."; 0 water charts. 404:budget: "Budget (0)" and "Nothing in budget needs attention."
findings.consequence: The overdue booster for 150 yearlings disappears and the page affirmatively says nothing in health needs attention. An empty water export removes both critical tank alerts (T2 low, T4 leak) and the page reports zero critical items. This is the most misleading failure mode because it looks like good news.
findings.regression_test: health.csv with the header and no rows, plus the tiny inline data. Expect a serious Health row or banner saying there is no health task data, and expect the Health chip count to be at least 1. water.csv with the header only: expect the tile not to read '0 of 0 | 0 need a look', and expect a row or banner saying there are no tank readings. These expectations are worked out by hand: an empty file is a data problem, not zero problems.
findings.proposed_fix: For each area, track whether data loaded (rows > 0 and the header matches). When it did not, add a serious 'No <area> data loaded (<file> empty or missing)' row, make the tile say 'no data', and let the 'Nothing in X needs attention' message appear only when that area's data is present.

findings.title: CSV text is injected through innerHTML: script from pasture names, tags and group names runs, and a payload can delete the alert rows
findings.location: app.js:28 (hover), app.js:54 (tile group names), app.js:68 (exception subject/problem), app.js:82 (water h4), app.js:104 (water tooltip), app.js:143 (grazing tooltip), app.js:170 (gain tooltip), app.js:194 (budget tooltip), app.js:198 (budget table)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASES R01-R04). Browser scenarios xss-onload, xss-tooltip, xss-hides-alerts. Example: data/pastures.csv with P4 named
findings.expected: CSV text shown as text, escaped as <img in innerHTML. No window.__xss_* flag set, and no injected elements.
findings.actual: Browser xss-onload: "xss flags: {\"pasture\":true,\"script\":false,\"tag\":true,\"group\":true,\"tip\":false}; injected elements: {\"img in #exceptions\":4,\"b in #exceptions\":1,\"img in #tiles\":1,\"img in #water h4\":1,\"script in #budgetTable\":1,\"total\":8}". Injected
findings.consequence: Anyone who can edit an upstream export (a pasture renamed in a shared sheet, a tag from a vendor system) can run script in the dashboard. The demonstrated payload empties the alert table while the chips still claim 10 problems, so a manager could miss a critical tank. Harmless names containing '<' get mangled too. In a portfolio piece, unescaped innerHTML of data is a well-known red flag for technical reviewers.
findings.regression_test: A pasture named 'x' with T2 steady at 20%. Expect the #exceptions innerHTML to contain '<b>x</b>' and not 'x'. Expect the T2 heading to contain '<b>'. A tag 't' on a hovered gain dot: expect the tooltip to contain '<i>t</i>'. Use the DOM stub harness in render.repro.mjs (cases R01-R04 flip to MATCH).
findings.proposed_fix: Add esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c])) and apply it to every CSV-derived value interpolated at the nine sinks. Alternatively, build table rows and tooltips with createElement and textContent. Keep the ICON SVGs as trusted constants.

findings.title: A tank with no reading in the last 7 days crashes the water charts and every section drawn after them
findings.location: app.js:90-93 (rows filtered to 7 days, then last.time on an empty array), app.js:225
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASE R13: T2 last readings 2026-09-21T06:00 and T12:00, as_of 2026-09-30T18:00). Browser scenario sensor-dead-8d (T6 rows after 2026-09-22T12:00 removed)
findings.expected: T2 listed as 'No reading for 222 hours' (Sep 21 12:00 to Sep 30 18:00 = 9 d 6 h, worked out by hand), and every section drawn, with T2's chart saying there is no data this week.
findings.actual: R13: T2 row "No reading for 222 hours; last level 70%" is shown, then "error=TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'time'); writes: water=0, grazing=0, gain=0, budgetTable=0, rules=0". Browser: uncaught ["Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'time')"], sections {"waterMinis":0,"grazingSvg":0,"gainSvg":0,"budgetSvg":0,"budgetRows":0,"rules":0} while the 10 exception rows are still shown.
findings.consequence: The sensor that has been dead longest, the tank most in need of a visit, wipes out all 8 water charts, the grazing rotation, the gain plot, the budget chart and table, and the rules table. The alert row survives, but the manager loses the context needed to plan the day.
findings.regression_test: The R13 data. Expect no error, the rules table written (12 tr: header + 11 rules, counted from app.js:203-215), 2 water mini charts, and T2's mini showing a 'no data' label. Expected hours worked out by hand: 222.
findings.proposed_fix: In waterMultiples, when rows is empty, skip the path and the dot and draw the 'no data in the last 7 days' wash over the whole chart. Isolate the sections with try/catch, as in the first finding.

findings.title: Infinity and NaN reach the display: a zero-budget category, an empty budget file and a missing budget file
findings.location: exceptions.js:88 (pct = variance / budget), exceptions.js:150, app.js:57 (tile), app.js:181-182 (lim = Infinity), app.js:198
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASES R14: add '2026-09,Drought feed,0,500'; R15: budget header-only and 404). Browser scenarios zero-budget-category, empty:budget, 404:budget
findings.expected: Unbudgeted spending reported in dollars (e.g. 'unbudgeted, $500'). No Infinity or NaN text, and no NaN SVG attributes. The tile says there is no budget data when the budget file is empty or missing.
findings.actual: R14: findExceptions problem "Infinity% over season to date ($500)"; 24 NaN/Infinity SVG attributes, e.g. ["<line x1=\"NaN\">","<line x2=\"NaN\">"]. Browser zero-budget-category: row "Serious | Budget | Drought feed | Infinity% over season to date ($3,200)"; 36 console errors such as "Error: <rect> attribute x: Expected length, \"NaN\"." R15: "header only: \"Spend vs budget: −NaN% | $0 of $0, season to date\"; 404: \"Spend vs budget: −NaN% | $NaN of $NaN, season to date\"; 404 budget table: [\"undefined | | $NaN | | $NaN | | $NaN |\"]"
findings.consequence: Unbudgeted spending, such as an emergency drought-feed purchase, is exactly what a manager must see. It shows as 'Infinity% over' and leaves every bar and gridline in the budget chart without a position. NaN tiles make the dashboard look broken to anyone evaluating it.
findings.regression_test: Budget rows Fuel 1000/1000 and Drought feed 0/500. Expect the problem text to contain '$500' and not 'Infinity'. Expect 0 NaN attributes in #budgetChart. Expect the Fuel bar at x(0) with width 1, since 0% over. A header-only budget: expect the tile text not to contain 'NaN'. Values worked out by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: In budgetStatus, set pct = budget > 0 ? variance / budget : null. In findExceptions, flag 'Unbudgeted: $X spent with no budget' when budget is 0 and actual is greater than 0. In budget(), compute lim over finite pct values only, and draw unbudgeted categories as a labelled dollar marker. In the tile, show 'no budget data' when tb is 0 or not finite.

findings.title: A blank tank level becomes a critical leak alarm: 'Dropped 70 points in 24 hours, now %'
findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (an empty cell stays ''), exceptions.js:49 (70 - '' = 70), exceptions.js:109-111, app.js:82
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASE R16: the last T2 row is 'T2,P2,2026-09-30T18:00,'). Browser scenario blank-level (T1's last level blank)
findings.expected: The blank is treated as a missing reading: T2 is judged on its last valid reading, 70% at 12:00, 6 h old, so no alert. Or it is reported as a sensor or data problem. Never 'now %'.
findings.actual:
R16: "exception: critical \"Dropped 70 points in 24 hours, now %\"; T2 chart heading: \"

T2 Windmill%

\"". Browser: "Critical | Water | Tank T1 (North Flat) | Dropped 100 points in 24 hours, now % | Check for a leak or a stuck float; haul water if it can't be fixed today", and the tile goes to "4 of 8 | 4 need a look".
findings.consequence: A single dropped sensor value sends someone to haul water to a full tank. False critical alarms erode trust in the report. This overlaps with the water and CSV audits; it is in scope here because the blank level reaches the display text.
findings.regression_test: The R16 data. Expect no critical row for T2 (worked out by hand: the last valid reading is 70% at 12:00, 6 h before as_of; under 24 h, so no silent rule; 70 is at or above 40, so no low rule). Expect the T2 heading to show 70%.
findings.proposed_fix: Before waterStatus, drop rows whose level_pct is not a finite number, or count them as missing readings so the silent-sensor rule can apply. Never interpolate an empty level into the alert text.

findings.title: 'Water tanks OK' tile parses the tank id back out of display text and undercounts ids containing a space
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASE R17: tanks 'Well 1' and 'Well 2', both steady at 20%). Browser scenario tank-ids-with-spaces (T2, T4, T6 renamed 'Well 2', 'Well 4', 'Well 6')
findings.expected: 'Water tanks OK: 0 of 2 | 2 need a look'. Worked out by hand: both are under 25%, giving 2 water rows.
findings.actual: R17: "\"Water tanks OK: 1 of 2 | 1 need a look\"; chip 'Water (2)'". Browser: tile "Water tanks OK: 7 of 8 | 1 need a look" while chips show "Water (3)" and there are 3 water rows.
findings.consequence: The at-a-glance number understates water problems, 1 instead of 3, for ranches that name tanks 'Well 2' or 'Windmill 4'. The tile and the chip disagree on the same screen.
findings.regression_test: The R17 data. Expect the tile to equal 'Water tanks OK: 0 of 2 | 2 need a look' and the Water chip to read 'Water (2)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a structured field (tank id) to water exceptions in findExceptions and count distinct ids from it, instead of parsing the display subject.

findings.title: Empty-state and zero-variance wording: 'Nothing in all needs attention.' and '−0.0%'
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASES R18, R19). Browser scenario all-clear (data edited so no rule fires; each chip clicked)
findings.expected: 'Nothing needs attention.' on the All filter. '0.0%' when spend equals budget (3000 of 3000, worked out by hand).
findings.actual: R18: "Nothing in all needs attention.". R19: "Spend vs budget: −0.0% | $3,000 of $3,000, season to date". Browser all-clear: tiles [..., "Spend vs budget: −0.0% | $88,400 of $88,400, season to date"]; messages [..., "Nothing in all needs attention."]
findings.consequence: Cosmetic, but the all-clear is the sentence a manager reads on a good day, and it reads as a template bug. A minus sign on exactly-on-budget suggests under-spending.
findings.regression_test: The clean tiny data. Expect the empty message to equal 'Nothing needs attention.'. Budget 1000/1000 and 2000/2000: expect the tile value to equal '0.0%'.
findings.proposed_fix: Use area === 'All' ? 'Nothing needs attention.' : `Nothing in ${area.toLowerCase()} needs attention.`, and set the sign to ta > tb ? '+' : ta < tb ? '−' : ''.

findings.title: Activating a filter chip drops keyboard focus to <body>
findings.location: app.js:62-65 (chips rebuilt with innerHTML on every click), app.js:224
findings.repro: Browser scenario chip-keyboard-focus in docs/audit/diagnostics/render.browser.mjs: focus #chips [data-a=Water], press Enter
findings.expected: The filter applies (3 rows) and focus stays on the Water chip.
findings.actual: measured: {"focusedAfterEnter":"BODY","rowsShown":3}. The filter works, but focus is lost; in a separate run a Tab afterwards landed on "All (10)".
findings.consequence: Keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place after each filter. It is minor operationally, but it is a visible quality gap in a portfolio piece.
findings.regression_test: Playwright: focus the Water chip, press Enter. Expect document.activeElement.dataset.a === 'Water', 3 data rows, and aria-pressed='true' on Water only.
findings.proposed_fix: Create the chips once. On click, update aria-pressed and the count labels in place instead of replacing the buttons.

findings.title: Tooltips run off-screen on a phone (water tooltip unclamped horizontally; all tooltips unclamped vertically)
findings.location: app.js:29-30 (hover() clamps only the left edge), app.js:105 (water tooltip clamps nothing)
findings.repro: Browser scenario tooltip-edges at a 390x844 viewport: hover the right edge of the right-column water chart, then a gain dot 20 px above the bottom of the viewport
findings.expected: The tooltip rect stays inside 0..innerWidth and 0..innerHeight.
findings.consequence: On a phone, the tank reading and the animal tag in a tooltip can be cut off, so the user has to reposition to read them.
findings.regression_test: Playwright at 390x844, using the same hover points. Expect tip.getBoundingClientRect().right <= 390 and .bottom <= 844.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one placeTip(e) helper for every tooltip that clamps both axes and flips above or left of the cursor near the edges.

findings.title: Grazing timeline month lines are hard-coded to June-September 2026
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/render.repro.mjs (CASE R20: tiny data whose season starts 2026-09-15)
findings.expected: Month lines only inside the plotted range [74, 550] and for months within the data's span.
findings.consequence: With any other season's data, the month labels are drawn outside the chart (svg.chart has overflow: visible) and the real months get no labels. It only shows up when real data replaces the fictional season.
findings.regression_test: Moves spanning 2027-05-01 to 2027-08-31. Expect month lines at 2027-06-01, 07-01 and 08-01 (worked out by hand), each with x between 74 and 550.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate the first of each month between the start date and as_of instead of using the literal list.

checked_ok: Baseline page is clean. Browser baseline: uncaught [], console errors (0), no NaN/undefined/Infinity on the page, all sections drawn ({"tiles":5,"chips":6,"exceptionTableRows":11,"waterMinis":8,"grazingSvg":1,"gainSvg":1,"budgetSvg":1,"budgetRows":7,"rules":12}).

Counts agree on the shipped data. render.repro C01: "tile=10, All chip=10, rows=10, area chips=[[\"Water\",3],[\"Grazing\",1],[\"Gain\",2],[\"Health\",2],[\"Budget\",2]] sum=10; NaN attrs=0". The severity split in the tile, "2 critical, 6 serious, 2 warning", matches the 10 browser rows.

Tiles match hand-computed values on tiny clean data. render.repro R00 MATCH: 'Head on grass: 13 | 10 cows, 3 yearlings', 'Yearling gain: 1.92 lbs/day' ((2+2+100/57)/3 = 1.918), 'Spend vs budget: −3.3% | $2,900 of $3,000'.

SVG chart labels go through textContent and are safe. render.repro C02 MATCH: "text node with the payload as plain text: true; #budgetChart innerHTML used: \"\"". The asof line also uses textContent (app.js:223).
Chips, severity badges and the rules table use only constants (AREAS, ICON, RULES text), so no CSV text reaches them.

A <script> element inserted through innerHTML does not execute. Browser xss-onload: script flag false although 'script in #budgetTable': 1. The other markup is still injected (see the innerHTML finding).
